# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 356
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/356
- **Title**: gh-349 parity: file_list/file_exists tools + lazy tracker in JSRunner + deterministic RetryPolicy (dm.ai#635)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-349` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +140
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T14:00:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T15:14:50Z

## PR Description

Closes #349
### What changed
Ported the deterministic-retry change from Java `RetryPolicy` (epam/dm.ai 3fa210e6, #635) and verified the other two items. `SyncRetryPolicy.isRetryableStatus`/`shouldRetry` now accept an optional response body: retryable by numeric status (429, 502/503/504) or a rate-limit/throttle body (`rate limit`, `too many requests`, `throttl`), never by substrings of an error message — the message embeds the request URL, so an ephemeral port like `50312` misfired the old `"503"` check and retried a 400. `SyncHttpClient` passes `resp.body` into the decision. Also aligned the JS-bridge `file_list` with Java `FileTools.listFiles` output (absolute, sorted `{"entries": [...]}`).

### Key decisions
- Ported the Java body-check branch exactly (case-insensitive, same three substrings); `statusCode == 0` stays an unconditional transport-failure retry.
- `file_list`/`file_exists` MCP catalog already matched the Java `@MCPTool` names/params — no catalog change; pinned the bridge behavior with `test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart`.
- Lazy tracker verified, no code change: `IntegrationClients` builds clients on first access (failure not cached); JS `jira_*` tools resolve config per call and fail on use with `Jira not configured` — `job_runner_test` runs scripts with all `JIRA_*` blanked.
- New tests mirror the Java `RetryPolicyTest` additions (URL port digits, retry by status/body).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/js/sync_http_retry_test.dart test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart
dart test            # full suite: 3646 passed, 16 skipped
crap4dart check --all  # 20 gates passed (coverage 96.7%), 1 pre-existing class_size warn
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[SyncHttpClient dispatch] --> POL[SyncRetryPolicy.shouldRetry]
  BODY[resp.body] --> POL
  POL -->|status 429/502/503/504| RETRY[retry with backoff]
  POL -->|body: rate limit / too many requests / throttl| RETRY
  POL -->|message/URL digits ignored| NORETRY[return response]
```
</details>

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 356
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/356
- **Title**: gh-349 parity: file_list/file_exists tools + lazy tracker in JSRunner + deterministic RetryPolicy (dm.ai#635)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-349` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +140
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T14:00:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T15:14:50Z

## PR Description

Closes #349
### What changed
Ported the deterministic-retry change from Java `RetryPolicy` (epam/dm.ai 3fa210e6, #635) and verified the other two items. `SyncRetryPolicy.isRetryableStatus`/`shouldRetry` now accept an optional response body: retryable by numeric status (429, 502/503/504) or a rate-limit/throttle body (`rate limit`, `too many requests`, `throttl`), never by substrings of an error message — the message embeds the request URL, so an ephemeral port like `50312` misfired the old `"503"` check and retried a 400. `SyncHttpClient` passes `resp.body` into the decision. Also aligned the JS-bridge `file_list` with Java `FileTools.listFiles` output (absolute, sorted `{"entries": [...]}`).

### Key decisions
- Ported the Java body-check branch exactly (case-insensitive, same three substrings); `statusCode == 0` stays an unconditional transport-failure retry.
- `file_list`/`file_exists` MCP catalog already matched the Java `@MCPTool` names/params — no catalog change; pinned the bridge behavior with `test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart`.
- Lazy tracker verified, no code change: `IntegrationClients` builds clients on first access (failure not cached); JS `jira_*` tools resolve config per call and fail on use with `Jira not configured` — `job_runner_test` runs scripts with all `JIRA_*` blanked.
- New tests mirror the Java `RetryPolicyTest` additions (URL port digits, retry by status/body).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/js/sync_http_retry_test.dart test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart
dart test            # full suite: 3646 passed, 16 skipped
crap4dart check --all  # 20 gates passed (coverage 96.7%), 1 pre-existing class_size warn
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[SyncHttpClient dispatch] --> POL[SyncRetryPolicy.shouldRetry]
  BODY[resp.body] --> POL
  POL -->|status 429/502/503/504| RETRY[retry with backoff]
  POL -->|body: rate limit / too many requests / throttl| RETRY
  POL -->|message/URL digits ignored| NORETRY[return response]
```
</details>

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local

If a successful response body contains "rate limit" (e.g., a Jira issue whose text contains "rate limit"), a 200 would be retried! Wait — shouldRetry(attempt, 200, body) → canRetryAfter(attempt) true, statusCode != 0, isRetryableStatus(200, body) → status not in the list, body contains "rate limit" → true → retry a successful 200! That's a real bug... unless Java behaves the same way. Does Java's isRetryable check status first and only check the body for certain statuses? Let me think about the old code: old `isRetryableStatus` returned true only for 429/502/503/504, so 200 never retried. New code: 200 with a body containing "rate limit" would be retried. Hmm, but wait — does the retry loop even call shouldRetry for 2xx? Looking at _dispatch: yes, for every response. Previously 2xx returned false from isRetryableStatus. Now a 200 with matching body would trigger retry, and `statusDelayMs(attempt, headers, 200)` → no Retry-After → backoff, then the loop repeats. On final attempt canRetryAfter false → return resp. So it would just add useless retries, not data loss, but it's a behavior change: successful requests with bodies containing "rate limit" get retried up to 5 times with backoff. Java parity matters — but even if Java has the same behavior... The test in the Java RetryPolicyTest — "testRestClientExceptionRetryableByStatusOrBody" — presumably tests an exception scenario, statuses 400 etc. In Java, is the body checked only when status is an error? I can't check Java source offline. Let me try web fetch of the Java file.

Actually, in practice: what 200 response body would contain "rate limit"? Jira GET issue could return body text containing "rate limit" in issue text. The client retries with sleeps. Result still correct but adds latency. Is that blocking? Java-parity is the spec (AGENTS.md rule 2: Java source is the spec). If Java does exactly this, it's parity and fine. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 356
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/356
- **Title**: gh-349 parity: file_list/file_exists tools + lazy tracker in JSRunner + deterministic RetryPolicy (dm.ai#635)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-349` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +140
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T14:00:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T15:14:50Z

## PR Description

Closes #349
### What changed
Ported the deterministic-retry change from Java `RetryPolicy` (epam/dm.ai 3fa210e6, #635) and verified the other two items. `SyncRetryPolicy.isRetryableStatus`/`shouldRetry` now accept an optional response body: retryable by numeric status (429, 502/503/504) or a rate-limit/throttle body (`rate limit`, `too many requests`, `throttl`), never by substrings of an error message — the message embeds the request URL, so an ephemeral port like `50312` misfired the old `"503"` check and retried a 400. `SyncHttpClient` passes `resp.body` into the decision. Also aligned the JS-bridge `file_list` with Java `FileTools.listFiles` output (absolute, sorted `{"entries": [...]}`).

### Key decisions
- Ported the Java body-check branch exactly (case-insensitive, same three substrings); `statusCode == 0` stays an unconditional transport-failure retry.
- `file_list`/`file_exists` MCP catalog already matched the Java `@MCPTool` names/params — no catalog change; pinned the bridge behavior with `test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart`.
- Lazy tracker verified, no code change: `IntegrationClients` builds clients on first access (failure not cached); JS `jira_*` tools resolve config per call and fail on use with `Jira not configured` — `job_runner_test` runs scripts with all `JIRA_*` blanked.
- New tests mirror the Java `RetryPolicyTest` additions (URL port digits, retry by status/body).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/js/sync_http_retry_test.dart test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart
dart test            # full suite: 3646 passed, 16 skipped
crap4dart check --all  # 20 gates passed (coverage 96.7%), 1 pre-existing class_size warn
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[SyncHttpClient dispatch] --> POL[SyncRetryPolicy.shouldRetry]
  BODY[resp.body] --> POL
  POL -->|status 429/502/503/504| RETRY[retry with backoff]
  POL -->|body: rate limit / too many requests / throttl| RETRY
  POL -->|message/URL digits ignored| NORETRY[return response]
```
</details>

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get

- **Title**: gh-349 parity: file_list/file_exists tools + lazy tracker in JSRunner + deterministic RetryPolicy (dm.ai#635)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-349` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +140
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T14:00:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T15:14:50Z

## PR Description

Closes #349
### What changed
Ported the deterministic-retry change from Java `RetryPolicy` (epam/dm.ai 3fa210e6, #635) and verified the other two items. `SyncRetryPolicy.isRetryableStatus`/`shouldRetry` now accept an optional response body: retryable by numeric status (429, 502/503/504) or a rate-limit/throttle body (`rate limit`, `too many requests`, `throttl`), never by substrings of an error message — the message embeds the request URL, so an ephemeral port like `50312` misfired the old `"503"` check and retried a 400. `SyncHttpClient` passes `resp.body` into the decision. Also aligned the JS-bridge `file_list` with Java `FileTools.listFiles` output (absolute, sorted `{"entries": [...]}`).

### Key decisions
- Ported the Java body-check branch exactly (case-insensitive, same three substrings); `statusCode == 0` stays an unconditional transport-failure retry.
- `file_list`/`file_exists` MCP catalog already matched the Java `@MCPTool` names/params — no catalog change; pinned the bridge behavior with `test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart`.
- Lazy tracker verified, no code change: `IntegrationClients` builds clients on first access (failure not cached); JS `jira_*` tools resolve config per call and fail on use with `Jira not configured` — `job_runner_test` runs scripts with all `JIRA_*` blanked.
- New tests mirror the Java `RetryPolicyTest` additions (URL port digits, retry by status/body).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/js/sync_http_retry_test.dart test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart
dart test            # full suite: 3646 passed, 16 skipped
crap4dart check --all  # 20 gates passed (coverage 96.7%), 1 pre-existing class_size warn
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[SyncHttpClient dispatch] --> POL[SyncRetryPolicy.shouldRetry]
  BODY[resp.body] --> POL
  POL -->|status 429/502/503/504| RETRY[retry with backoff]
  POL -->|body: rate limit / too many requests / throttl| RETRY
  POL -->|message/URL digits ignored| NORETRY[return response]
```
</details>

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local

Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 356
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/356
- **Title**: gh-349 parity: file_list/file_exists tools + lazy tracker in JSRunner + deterministic RetryPolicy (dm.ai#635)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-349` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +140
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T14:00:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T15:14:50Z

## PR Description

Closes #349
### What changed
Ported the deterministic-retry change from Java `RetryPolicy` (epam/dm.ai 3fa210e6, #635) and verified the other two items. `SyncRetryPolicy.isRetryableStatus`/`shouldRetry` now accept an optional response body: retryable by numeric status (429, 502/503/504) or a rate-limit/throttle body (`rate limit`, `too many requests`, `throttl`), never by substrings of an error message — the message embeds the request URL, so an ephemeral port like `50312` misfired the old `"503"` check and retried a 400. `SyncHttpClient` passes `resp.body` into the decision. Also aligned the JS-bridge `file_list` with Java `FileTools.listFiles` output (absolute, sorted `{"entries": [...]}`).

### Key decisions
- Ported the Java body-check branch exactly (case-insensitive, same three substrings); `statusCode == 0` stays an unconditional transport-failure retry.
- `file_list`/`file_exists` MCP catalog already matched the Java `@MCPTool` names/params — no catalog change; pinned the bridge behavior with `test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart`.
- Lazy tracker verified, no code change: `IntegrationClients` builds clients on first access (failure not cached); JS `jira_*` tools resolve config per call and fail on use with `Jira not configured` — `job_runner_test` runs scripts with all `JIRA_*` blanked.
- New tests mirror the Java `RetryPolicyTest` additions (URL port digits, retry by status/body).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/js/sync_http_retry_test.dart test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart
dart test            # full suite: 3646 passed, 16 skipped
crap4dart check --all  # 20 gates passed (coverage 96.7%), 1 pre-existing class_size warn
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[SyncHttpClient dispatch] --> POL[SyncRetryPolicy.shouldRetry]
  BODY[resp.body] --> POL
  POL -->|status 429/502/503/504| RETRY[retry with backoff]
  POL -->|body: rate limit / too many requests / throttl| RETRY
  POL -->|message/URL digits ignored| NORETRY[return response]
```
</details>

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 356
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/356
- **Title**: gh-349 parity: file_list/file_exists tools + lazy tracker in JSRunner + deterministic RetryPolicy (dm.ai#635)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-349` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +140
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T14:00:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T15:14:50Z

## PR Description

Closes #349
### What changed
Ported the deterministic-retry change from Java `RetryPolicy` (epam/dm.ai 3fa210e6, #635) and verified the other two items. `SyncRetryPolicy.isRetryableStatus`/`shouldRetry` now accept an optional response body: retryable by numeric status (429, 502/503/504) or a rate-limit/throttle body (`rate limit`, `too many requests`, `throttl`), never by substrings of an error message — the message embeds the request URL, so an ephemeral port like `50312` misfired the old `"503"` check and retried a 400. `SyncHttpClient` passes `resp.body` into the decision. Also aligned the JS-bridge `file_list` with Java `FileTools.listFiles` output (absolute, sorted `{"entries": [...]}`).

### Key decisions
- Ported the Java body-check branch exactly (case-insensitive, same three substrings); `statusCode == 0` stays an unconditional transport-failure retry.
- `file_list`/`file_exists` MCP catalog already matched the Java `@MCPTool` names/params — no catalog change; pinned the bridge behavior with `test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart`.
- Lazy tracker verified, no code change: `IntegrationClients` builds clients on first access (failure not cached); JS `jira_*` tools resolve config per call and fail on use with `Jira not configured` — `job_runner_test` runs scripts with all `JIRA_*` blanked.
- New tests mirror the Java `RetryPolicyTest` additions (URL port digits, retry by status/body).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/js/sync_http_retry_test.dart test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart
dart test            # full suite: 3646 passed, 16 skipped
crap4dart check --all  # 20 gates passed (coverage 96.7%), 1 pre-existing class_size warn
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[SyncHttpClient dispatch] --> POL[SyncRetryPolicy.shouldRetry]
  BODY[resp.body] --> POL
  POL -->|status 429/502/503/504| RETRY[retry with backoff]
  POL -->|body: rate limit / too many requests / throttl| RETRY
  POL -->|message/URL digits ignored| NORETRY[return response]
```
</details>

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 356
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/356
- **Title**: gh-349 parity: file_list/file_exists tools + lazy tracker in JSRunner + deterministic RetryPolicy (dm.ai#635)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-349` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +140
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T14:00:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T15:14:50Z

## PR Description

Closes #349
### What changed
Ported the deterministic-retry change from Java `RetryPolicy` (epam/dm.ai 3fa210e6, #635) and verified the other two items. `SyncRetryPolicy.isRetryableStatus`/`shouldRetry` now accept an optional response body: retryable by numeric status (429, 502/503/504) or a rate-limit/throttle body (`rate limit`, `too many requests`, `throttl`), never by substrings of an error message — the message embeds the request URL, so an ephemeral port like `50312` misfired the old `"503"` check and retried a 400. `SyncHttpClient` passes `resp.body` into the decision. Also aligned the JS-bridge `file_list` with Java `FileTools.listFiles` output (absolute, sorted `{"entries": [...]}`).

### Key decisions
- Ported the Java body-check branch exactly (case-insensitive, same three substrings); `statusCode == 0` stays an unconditional transport-failure retry.
- `file_list`/`file_exists` MCP catalog already matched the Java `@MCPTool` names/params — no catalog change; pinned the bridge behavior with `test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart`.
- Lazy tracker verified, no code change: `IntegrationClients` builds clients on first access (failure not cached); JS `jira_*` tools resolve config per call and fail on use with `Jira not configured` — `job_runner_test` runs scripts with all `JIRA_*` blanked.
- New tests mirror the Java `RetryPolicyTest` additions (URL port digits, retry by status/body).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/js/sync_http_retry_test.dart test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart
dart test            # full suite: 3646 passed, 16 skipped
crap4dart check --all  # 20 gates passed (coverage 96.7%), 1 pre-existing class_size warn
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[SyncHttpClient dispatch] --> POL[SyncRetryPolicy.shouldRetry]
  BODY[resp.body] --> POL
  POL -->|status 429/502/503/504| RETRY[retry with backoff]
  POL -->|body: rate limit / too many requests / throttl| RETRY
  POL -->|message/URL digits ignored| NORETRY[return response]
```
</details>

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 356
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/356
- **Title**: gh-349 parity: file_list/file_exists tools + lazy tracker in JSRunner + deterministic RetryPolicy (dm.ai#635)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-349` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +140
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T14:00:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T15:14:50Z

## PR Description

Closes #349
### What changed
Ported the deterministic-retry change from Java `RetryPolicy` (epam/dm.ai 3fa210e6, #635) and verified the other two items. `SyncRetryPolicy.isRetryableStatus`/`shouldRetry` now accept an optional response body: retryable by numeric status (429, 502/503/504) or a rate-limit/throttle body (`rate limit`, `too many requests`, `throttl`), never by substrings of an error message — the message embeds the request URL, so an ephemeral port like `50312` misfired the old `"503"` check and retried a 400. `SyncHttpClient` passes `resp.body` into the decision. Also aligned the JS-bridge `file_list` with Java `FileTools.listFiles` output (absolute, sorted `{"entries": [...]}`).

### Key decisions
- Ported the Java body-check branch exactly (case-insensitive, same three substrings); `statusCode == 0` stays an unconditional transport-failure retry.
- `file_list`/`file_exists` MCP catalog already matched the Java `@MCPTool` names/params — no catalog change; pinned the bridge behavior with `test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart`.
- Lazy tracker verified, no code change: `IntegrationClients` builds clients on first access (failure not cached); JS `jira_*` tools resolve config per call and fail on use with `Jira not configured` — `job_runner_test` runs scripts with all `JIRA_*` blanked.
- New tests mirror the Java `RetryPolicyTest` additions (URL port digits, retry by status/body).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/js/sync_http_retry_test.dart test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart
dart test            # full suite: 3646 passed, 16 skipped
crap4dart check --all  # 20 gates passed (coverage 96.7%), 1 pre-existing class_size warn
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[SyncHttpClient dispatch] --> POL[SyncRetryPolicy.shouldRetry]
  BODY[resp.body] --> POL
  POL -->|status 429/502/503/504| RETRY[retry with backoff]
  POL -->|body: rate limit / too many requests / throttl| RETRY
  POL -->|message/URL digits ignored| NORETRY[return response]
```
</details>

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local

1. `isRetryableStatus` with body: In Java, does the body check apply even for non-retryable statuses like 404? The port says status in {429,502,503,504} → true; else check body. So a 404 with body "rate limit" would retry. Let me check the Java implementation to verify parity. The PR says "port the deterministic policy exactly." Test expects `policy.shouldRetry(1, 404, 'nope')` is false and `shouldRetry(1, 400, 'Too Many Requests')` is true. Is the Java behavior really: any status with a rate-limit body is retryable? Let me fetch the Java source from epam/dm.ai... That may not be accessible. Try web fetch or check if there's a local clone of dependencies. The review note says Java source is the spec. Let me try to find RetryPolicy.java.

2. The `_listDir` change: `File(e.path).absolute.path` — does File.absolute normalize? `File(path).absolute` returns a File with the path made absolute, but does NOT normalize `.`/`..` segments. The comment says "absolute, normalized, and sorted". Actually `File.absolute` in Dart just prepends Directory.current if not already absolute — normalization. Since `_resolve` already prepends the base for relative paths, e.path from `Directory(_resolve(path)).listSync()` will already be absolute (since the dir path is absolute). So `.absolute.path` is mostly a no-op unless... Actually wait — `Directory('/abs').listSync()` returns entities with paths like '/abs/entry' — absolute already. And `_resolve` makes paths absolute. So `File(e.path).absolute.path` is redundant in most cases but harmless. But it does NOT normalize `.`/`..` segments, contradicting the "normalized" comment. Minor doc/behavior nit — SUGGESTION at most. Actually is it possible that `path` passed to Directory contains segments like `/tmp/foo/../bar`? Then listSync returns paths containing `..` still. Java's getCanonicalPath or normalize? FileTools.listFiles — can't verify without Java source. This is a minor issue.

3. Lazy tracker: verified no code change. Ticket item 2 asked to verify laziness; PR description says verified. OK.

4. `file_list`/`file_exists` catalog parity — verified matching, pinned by tests. OK.

5. Backward compatibility: `shouldRetry` and `isRetryableStatus` gained optional params — backward compatible. SyncHttpClient passes body. Other callers? Only sync_http_client and tests. Good.

6. One potential issue: body-based retry applies regardless of status — a 200 response with body containing "throttl"? In _dispatch, `shouldRetry` is called on every response including 2xx. If a successful response body contains "rate limit" (e.g., a Jira issue whose text contains "rate limit"), a 200 would be retried! Wait — shouldRetry(attempt, 200, body) → canRetryAfter(attempt) true, statusCode != 0, isRetryableStatus(200, body) → status not in the list, body contains "rate limit" → true → retry a successful 200! That's a real bug... unless Java behaves the same way. Does Java's isRetryable check status first and only check the body for certain statuses? Let me think about the old code: old `isRetryableStatus` returned true only for 429/502/503/504, so 200 never retried. New code: 200 with a body containing "rate limit" would be retried. Hmm, but wait — does the retry loop even call shouldRetry for 2xx? Looking at _dispatch: yes, for every response. Previously 2xx returned false from isRetryableStatus. Now a 200 with matching body would trigger retry, and `statusDelayMs(attempt, headers, 200)` → no Retry-After → backoff, then the loop repeats. On final attempt canRetryAfter false → return resp. So it would just add useless retries, not data loss, but it's a behavior change: successful requests with bodies containing "rate limit" get retried up to 5 times with backoff. Java parity matters — but even if Java has the same behavior... The test in the Java RetryPolicyTest — "testRestClientExceptionRetryableByStatusOrBody" — presumably tests an exception scenario, statuses 400 etc. In Java, is the body checked only when status is an error? I can't check Java source offline. Let me try web fetch of the Java file.

Actually, in practice: what 200 response body would contain "rate limit"? Jira GET issue could return body text containing "rate limit" in issue text. The client retries with sleeps. Result still correct but adds latency. Is that blocking? Java-parity is the spec (AGENTS.md rule 2: Java source is the spec). If Java does exactly this, it's parity and fine. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 356
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/356
- **Title**: gh-349 parity: file_list/file_exists tools + lazy tracker in JSRunner + deterministic RetryPolicy (dm.ai#635)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-349` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +140
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T14:00:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T15:14:50Z

## PR Description

Closes #349
### What changed
Ported the deterministic-retry change from Java `RetryPolicy` (epam/dm.ai 3fa210e6, #635) and verified the other two items. `SyncRetryPolicy.isRetryableStatus`/`shouldRetry` now accept an optional response body: retryable by numeric status (429, 502/503/504) or a rate-limit/throttle body (`rate limit`, `too many requests`, `throttl`), never by substrings of an error message — the message embeds the request URL, so an ephemeral port like `50312` misfired the old `"503"` check and retried a 400. `SyncHttpClient` passes `resp.body` into the decision. Also aligned the JS-bridge `file_list` with Java `FileTools.listFiles` output (absolute, sorted `{"entries": [...]}`).

### Key decisions
- Ported the Java body-check branch exactly (case-insensitive, same three substrings); `statusCode == 0` stays an unconditional transport-failure retry.
- `file_list`/`file_exists` MCP catalog already matched the Java `@MCPTool` names/params — no catalog change; pinned the bridge behavior with `test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart`.
- Lazy tracker verified, no code change: `IntegrationClients` builds clients on first access (failure not cached); JS `jira_*` tools resolve config per call and fail on use with `Jira not configured` — `job_runner_test` runs scripts with all `JIRA_*` blanked.
- New tests mirror the Java `RetryPolicyTest` additions (URL port digits, retry by status/body).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/js/sync_http_retry_test.dart test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart
dart test            # full suite: 3646 passed, 16 skipped
crap4dart check --all  # 20 gates passed (coverage 96.7%), 1 pre-existing class_size warn
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[SyncHttpClient dispatch] --> POL[SyncRetryPolicy.shouldRetry]
  BODY[resp.body] --> POL
  POL -->|status 429/502/503/504| RETRY[retry with backoff]
  POL -->|body: rate limit / too many requests / throttl| RETRY
  POL -->|message/URL digits ignored| NORETRY[return response]
```
</details>

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
