blocks.text:
Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 356
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/356
- **Title**: gh-349 parity: file_list/file_exists tools + lazy tracker in JSRunner + deterministic RetryPolicy (dm.ai#635)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-349` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +140
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T14:00:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T15:14:50Z

## PR Description

Closes #349
### What changed
Ported the deterministic-retry change from Java `RetryPolicy` (epam/dm.ai 3fa210e6, #635) and verified the other two items. `SyncRetryPolicy.isRetryableStatus`/`shouldRetry` now accept an optional response body: retryable by numeric status (429, 502/503/504) or a rate-limit/throttle body (`rate limit`, `too many requests`, `throttl`), never by substrings of an error message — the message embeds the request URL, so an ephemeral port like `50312` misfired the old `"503"` check and retried a 400. `SyncHttpClient` passes `resp.body` into the decision. Also aligned the JS-bridge `file_list` with Java `FileTools.listFiles` output (absolute, sorted `{"entries": [...]}`).

### Key decisions
- Ported the Java body-check branch exactly (case-insensitive, same three substrings); `statusCode == 0` stays an unconditional transport-failure retry.
- `file_list`/`file_exists` MCP catalog already matched the Java `@MCPTool` names/params — no catalog change; pinned the bridge behavior with `test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart`.
- Lazy tracker verified, no code change: `IntegrationClients` builds clients on first access (failure not cached); JS `jira_*` tools resolve config per call and fail on use with `Jira not configured` — `job_runner_test` runs scripts with all `JIRA_*` blanked.
- New tests mirror the Java `RetryPolicyTest` additions (URL port digits, retry by status/body).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/js/sync_http_retry_test.dart test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart
dart test            # full suite: 3646 passed, 16 skipped
crap4dart check --all  # 20 gates passed (coverage 96.7%), 1 pre-existing class_size warn
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[SyncHttpClient dispatch] --> POL[SyncRetryPolicy.shouldRetry]
  BODY[resp.body] --> POL
  POL -->|status 429/502/503/504| RETRY[retry with backoff]
  POL -->|body: rate limit / too many requests / throttl| RETRY
  POL -->|message/URL digits ignored| NORETRY[return response]
```
</details>

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 356
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/356
- **Title**: gh-349 parity: file_list/file_exists tools + lazy tracker in JSRunner + deterministic RetryPolicy (dm.ai#635)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-349` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +140
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T14:00:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T15:14:50Z

## PR Description

Closes #349
### What changed
Ported the deterministic-retry change from Java `RetryPolicy` (epam/dm.ai 3fa210e6, #635) and verified the other two items. `SyncRetryPolicy.isRetryableStatus`/`shouldRetry` now accept an optional response body: retryable by numeric status (429, 502/503/504) or a rate-limit/throttle body (`rate limit`, `too many requests`, `throttl`), never by substrings of an error message — the message embeds the request URL, so an ephemeral port like `50312` misfired the old `"503"` check and retried a 400. `SyncHttpClient` passes `resp.body` into the decision. Also aligned the JS-bridge `file_list` with Java `FileTools.listFiles` output (absolute, sorted `{"entries": [...]}`).

### Key decisions
- Ported the Java body-check branch exactly (case-insensitive, same three substrings); `statusCode == 0` stays an unconditional transport-failure retry.
- `file_list`/`file_exists` MCP catalog already matched the Java `@MCPTool` names/params — no catalog change; pinned the bridge behavior with `test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart`.
- Lazy tracker verified, no code change: `IntegrationClients` builds clients on first access (failure not cached); JS `jira_*` tools resolve config per call and fail on use with `Jira not configured` — `job_runner_test` runs scripts with all `JIRA_*` blanked.
- New tests mirror the Java `RetryPolicyTest` additions (URL port digits, retry by status/body).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/js/sync_http_retry_test.dart test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart
dart test            # full suite: 3646 passed, 16 skipped
crap4dart check --all  # 20 gates passed (coverage 96.7%), 1 pre-existing class_size warn
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[SyncHttpClient dispatch] --> POL[SyncRetryPolicy.shouldRetry]
  BODY[resp.body] --> POL
  POL -->|status 429/502/503/504| RETRY[retry with backoff]
  POL -->|body: rate limit / too many requests / throttl| RETRY
  POL -->|message/URL digits ignored| NORETRY[return response]
```

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 356
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/356
- **Title**: gh-349 parity: file_list/file_exists tools + lazy tracker in JSRunner + deterministic RetryPolicy (dm.ai#635)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-349` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +140
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T14:00:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T15:14:50Z

## PR Description

Closes #349
### What changed
Ported the deterministic-retry change from Java `RetryPolicy` (epam/dm.ai 3fa210e6, #635) and verified the other two items. `SyncRetryPolicy.isRetryableStatus`/`shouldRetry` now accept an optional response body: retryable by numeric status (429, 502/503/504) or a rate-limit/throttle body (`rate limit`, `too many requests`, `throttl`), never by substrings of an error message — the message embeds the request URL, so an ephemeral port like `50312` misfired the old `"503"` check and retried a 400. `SyncHttpClient` passes `resp.body` into the decision. Also aligned the JS-bridge `file_list` with Java `FileTools.listFiles` output (absolute, sorted `{"entries": [...]}`).

### Key decisions
- Ported the Java body-check branch exactly (case-insensitive, same three substrings); `statusCode == 0` stays an unconditional transport-failure retry.
- `file_list`/`file_exists` MCP catalog already matched the Java `@MCPTool` names/params — no catalog change; pinned the bridge behavior with `test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart`.
- Lazy tracker verified, no code change: `IntegrationClients` builds clients on first access (failure not cached); JS `jira_*` tools resolve config per call and fail on use with `Jira not configured` — `job_runner_test` runs scripts with all `JIRA_*` blanked.
- New tests mirror the Java `RetryPolicyTest` additions (URL port digits, retry by status/body).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/js/sync_http_retry_test.dart test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart
dart test            # full suite: 3646 passed, 16 skipped
crap4dart check --all  # 20 gates passed (coverage 96.7%), 1 pre-existing class_size warn
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[SyncHttpClient dispatch] --> POL[SyncRetryPolicy.shouldRetry]
  BODY[resp.body] --> POL
  POL -->|status 429/502/503/504| RETRY[retry with backoff]
  POL -->|body: rate limit / too many requests / throttl| RETRY
  POL -->|message/URL digits ignored| NORETRY[return response]
```
</details>

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local

Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 356
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/356
- **Title**: gh-349 parity: file_list/file_exists tools + lazy tracker in JSRunner + deterministic RetryPolicy (dm.ai#635)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-349` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +140
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T14:00:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T15:14:50Z

## PR Description

Closes #349
### What changed
Ported the deterministic-retry change from Java `RetryPolicy` (epam/dm.ai 3fa210e6, #635) and verified the other two items. `SyncRetryPolicy.isRetryableStatus`/`shouldRetry` now accept an optional response body: retryable by numeric status (429, 502/503/504) or a rate-limit/throttle body (`rate limit`, `too many requests`, `throttl`), never by substrings of an error message — the message embeds the request URL, so an ephemeral port like `50312` misfired the old `"503"` check and retried a 400. `SyncHttpClient` passes `resp.body` into the decision. Also aligned the JS-bridge `file_list` with Java `FileTools.listFiles` output (absolute, sorted `{"entries": [...]}`).

### Key decisions
- Ported the Java body-check branch exactly (case-insensitive, same three substrings); `statusCode == 0` stays an unconditional transport-failure retry.
- `file_list`/`file_exists` MCP catalog already matched the Java `@MCPTool` names/params — no catalog change; pinned the bridge behavior with `test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart`.
- Lazy tracker verified, no code change: `IntegrationClients` builds clients on first access (failure not cached); JS `jira_*` tools resolve config per call and fail on use with `Jira not configured` — `job_runner_test` runs scripts with all `JIRA_*` blanked.
- New tests mirror the Java `RetryPolicyTest` additions (URL port digits, retry by status/body).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/js/sync_http_retry_test.dart test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart
dart test            # full suite: 3646 passed, 16 skipped
crap4dart check --all  # 20 gates passed (coverage 96.7%), 1 pre-existing class_size warn
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[SyncHttpClient dispatch] --> POL[SyncRetryPolicy.shouldRetry]
  BODY[resp.body] --> POL
  POL -->|status 429/502/503/504| RETRY[retry with backoff]
  POL -->|body: rate limit / too many requests / throttl| RETRY
  POL -->|message/URL digits ignored| NORETRY[return response]
```
</details>

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).

content.thinking:
Java `isRetryableStatus(RestClientException)` checks: status in {429,502,503,504} OR body contains rate-limit substrings — exactly what the Dart port does. In Java, isRetryable is only called for exceptions (failed requests), never for 2xx responses. In Dart's `_dispatch`, `shouldRetry` is called for every response including 2xx. The port, as applied, means: a 2xx response whose body contains "rate limit" will now be retried (up to 5 attempts with backoff). Previously 2xx never retried.

Wait — is that true? In old Dart code, `isRetryableStatus(200)` returned false → no retry. New code: `isRetryableStatus(200, body)` — status check fails, then body check: if body contains "rate limit" → true → retry. Yes, a 200 with matching body retries. That's a genuine behavioral divergence introduced by this port: Java only checks bodies on exceptions (error responses); Dart applies body-matching to all responses.

How impactful? GET issue from Jira: issue text/description might include "rate limit". Response 200. Client retries with backoff — up to 4 wasted sleeps (up to 60s total), result still correct. It's a correctness/performance issue but not data loss. Is it blocking? Given the loop is on all methods and a 200-body containing "throttl" etc. occurs in real content (e.g., searching Jira for tickets about rate limits — JQL search results returning issues whose summary contains "rate limit"!). That's plausible: `jira_search_by_jql` on text ~"rate limit" would return 200 with body containing "rate limit" → every such request retried 5x with exponential backoff up to 60s each. That's a significant latency bug for a plausible scenario.

But wait — Java parity is the spec. In Java, the check happens in `isRetryable(IOException)` — only invoked in catch block. The Dart structure differs (no exceptions, status-code based). The faithful port of intent would gate body-matching to non-2xx statuses, e.g. only when statusCode >= 400, or at least `!resp.isOk`. Actually Java's `isClientError` note... the cleanest: in `_dispatch` or `shouldRetry`, return false for 2xx. Since shouldRetry(attempt, 200, body) — old behavior false for all 2xx. I'd flag this as IMPORTANT (maybe BLOCKING? It causes unnecessary multi-minute delays for real queries; but not data corruption). Let me consider severity: retry of a 200 is wasted work + latency, worst case adds ~60s+ to requests. Jira cloud GET requests with such content would be slowed significantly. I'd classify IMPORTANT (correctness/performance), borderline. Hmm, per guidelines "BLOCKING — merge would cause a bug". Retrying successful 200s is a bug. It doesn't corrupt data though. I'll classify IMPORTANT... Actually let me think about how likely a 200 body contains "rate limit": JQL search results for tracker tooling, issue comments mentioning rate limits — quite plausible. Each retry sleeps up to 60s (backoff 1s,2s,4s,8s capped... maxDelayMs 600; attempts 5 → 1+2+4+8+16s=31s typical). That makes affected API calls 30+s slower. That's a real user-facing regression for a plausible input. I'll go BLOCKING? The instructions say "When in doubt, start one level higher". A request that returns 200 being retried is objectively wrong behavior introduced by this diff. I'll mark it BLOCKING.

Fix suggestion: gate body-check behind error statuses:
```dart
bool isRetryableStatus(int status, [String? body]) {
  if (status == 429 || status == 502 || status == 503 || status == 504) return true;
  if (status < 400) return false; // 2xx/3xx success: never retry
  ...
}
```
Or in shouldRetry: `if (statusCode >= 200 && statusCode < 400) return false;`. Test: `expect(policy.shouldRetry(1, 200, 'rate limit docs'), isFalse)`.

Also, `File(...)` for directory entries is odd — should use `FileSystemEntity` or `p.absolute`. Since `_resolve` already makes the dir path absolute, entries are already absolute; `.absolute` is a near-no-op. Minor: SUGGESTION. ## PR Description

Closes #349
### What changed
Ported the deterministic-retry change from Java `RetryPolicy` (epam/dm.ai 3fa210e6, #635) and verified the other two items. `SyncRetryPolicy.isRetryableStatus`/`shouldRetry` now accept an optional response body: retryable by numeric status (429, 502/503/504) or a rate-limit/throttle body (`rate limit`, `too many requests`, `throttl`), never by substrings of an error message — the message embeds the request URL, so an ephemeral port like `50312` misfired the old `"503"` check and retried a 400. `SyncHttpClient` passes `resp.body` into the decision. Also aligned the JS-bridge `file_list` with Java `FileTools.listFiles` output (absolute, sorted `{"entries": [...]}`).

### Key decisions
- Ported the Java body-check branch exactly (case-insensitive, same three substrings); `statusCode == 0` stays an unconditional transport-failure retry.
- `file_list`/`file_exists` MCP catalog already matched the Java `@MCPTool` names/params — no catalog change; pinned the bridge behavior with `test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart`.
- Lazy tracker verified, no code change: `IntegrationClients` builds clients on first access (failure not cached); JS `jira_*` tools resolve config per call and fail on use with `Jira not configured` — `job_runner_test` runs scripts with all `JIRA_*` blanked.
- New tests mirror the Java `RetryPolicyTest` additions (URL port digits, retry by status/body).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/js/sync_http_retry_test.dart test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart
dart test            # full suite: 3646 passed, 16 skipped
crap4dart check --all  # 20 gates passed (coverage 96.7%), 1 pre-existing class_size warn
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[SyncHttpClient dispatch] --> POL[SyncRetryPolicy.shouldRetry]
  BODY[resp.body] --> POL
  POL -->|status 429/502/503/504| RETRY[retry with backoff]
  POL -->|body: rate limit / too many requests / throttl| RETRY
  POL -->|message/URL digits ignored| NORETRY[return response]
```
</details>

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local

blocks.text:
Java `isRetryableStatus(RestClientException)` checks: status in {429,502,503,504} OR body contains rate-limit substrings — exactly what the Dart port does. In Java, isRetryable is only called for exceptions (failed requests), never for 2xx responses. In Dart's `_dispatch`, `shouldRetry` is called for every response including 2xx. The port, as applied, means: a 2xx response whose body contains "rate limit" will now be retried (up to 5 attempts with backoff). Previously 2xx never retried.

Wait — is that true? In old Dart code, `isRetryableStatus(200)` returned false → no retry. New code: `isRetryableStatus(200, body)` — status check fails, then body check: if body contains "rate limit" → true → retry. Yes, a 200 with matching body retries. That's a genuine behavioral divergence introduced by this port: Java only checks bodies on exceptions (error responses); Dart applies body-matching to all responses.

How impactful? GET issue from Jira: issue text/description might include "rate limit". Response 200. Client retries with backoff — up to 4 wasted sleeps (up to 60s total), result still correct. It's a correctness/performance issue but not data loss. Is it blocking? Given the loop is on all methods and a 200-body containing "throttl" etc. occurs in real content (e.g., searching Jira for tickets about rate limits — JQL search results returning issues whose summary contains "rate limit"!). That's plausible: `jira_search_by_jql` on text ~"rate limit" would return 200 with body containing "rate limit" → every such request retried 5x with exponential backoff up to 60s each. That's a significant latency bug for a plausible scenario.

But wait — Java parity is the spec. In Java, the check happens in `isRetryable(IOException)` — only invoked in catch block. The Dart structure differs (no exceptions, status-code based). The faithful port of intent would gate body-matching to non-2xx statuses, e.g. only when statusCode >= 400, or at least `!resp.isOk`. Actually Java's `isClientError` note... the cleanest: in `_dispatch` or `shouldRetry`, return false for 2xx. Since shouldRetry(attempt, 200, body) — old behavior false for all 2xx. I'd flag this as IMPORTANT (maybe BLOCKING? It causes unnecessary multi-minute delays for real queries; but not data corruption). Let me consider severity: retry of a 200 is wasted work + latency, worst case adds ~60s+ to requests. Jira cloud GET requests with such content would be slowed significantly. I'd classify IMPORTANT (correctness/performance), borderline. Hmm, per guidelines "BLOCKING — merge would cause a bug". Retrying successful 200s is a bug. It doesn't corrupt data though. I'll classify IMPORTANT... Actually let me think about how likely a 200 body contains "rate limit": JQL search results for tracker tooling, issue comments mentioning rate limits — quite plausible. Each retry sleeps up to 60s (backoff 1s,2s,4s,8s capped... maxDelayMs 600; attempts 5 → 1+2+4+8+16s=31s typical). That makes affected API calls 30+s slower. That's a real user-facing regression for a plausible input. I'll go BLOCKING? The instructions say "When in doubt, start one level higher". A request that returns 200 being retried is objectively wrong behavior introduced by this diff. I'll mark it BLOCKING.

}

## PR Description

Closes #349
### What changed
Ported the deterministic-retry change from Java `RetryPolicy` (epam/dm.ai 3fa210e6, #635) and verified the other two items. `SyncRetryPolicy.isRetryableStatus`/`shouldRetry` now accept an optional response body: retryable by numeric status (429, 502/503/504) or a rate-limit/throttle body (`rate limit`, `too many requests`, `throttl`), never by substrings of an error message — the message embeds the request URL, so an ephemeral port like `50312` misfired the old `"503"` check and retried a 400. `SyncHttpClient` passes `resp.body` into the decision. Also aligned the JS-bridge `file_list` with Java `FileTools.listFiles` output (absolute, sorted `{"entries": [...]}`).

### Key decisions
- Ported the Java body-check branch exactly (case-insensitive, same three substrings); `statusCode == 0` stays an unconditional transport-failure retry.
- `file_list`/`file_exists` MCP catalog already matched the Java `@MCPTool` names/params — no catalog change; pinned the bridge behavior with `test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart`.
- Lazy tracker verified, no code change: `IntegrationClients` builds clients on first access (failure not cached); JS `jira_*` tools resolve config per call and fail on use with `Jira not configured` — `job_runner_test` runs scripts with all `JIRA_*` blanked.
- New tests mirror the Java `RetryPolicyTest` additions (URL port digits, retry by status/body).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/js/sync_http_retry_test.dart test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart
dart test            # full suite: 3646 passed, 16 skipped
crap4dart check --all  # 20 gates passed (coverage 96.7%), 1 pre-existing class_size warn
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[SyncHttpClient dispatch] --> POL[SyncRetryPolicy.shouldRetry]
  BODY[resp.body] --> POL
  POL -->|status 429/502/503/504| RETRY[retry with backoff]
  POL -->|body: rate limit / too many requests / throttl| RETRY
  POL -->|message/URL digits ignored| NORETRY[return response]
```
</details>

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local

## PR Description

Closes #349
### What changed
Ported the deterministic-retry change from Java `RetryPolicy` (epam/dm.ai 3fa210e6, #635) and verified the other two items. `SyncRetryPolicy.isRetryableStatus`/`shouldRetry` now accept an optional response body: retryable by numeric status (429, 502/503/504) or a rate-limit/throttle body (`rate limit`, `too many requests`, `throttl`), never by substrings of an error message — the message embeds the request URL, so an ephemeral port like `50312` misfired the old `"503"` check and retried a 400. `SyncHttpClient` passes `resp.body` into the decision. Also aligned the JS-bridge `file_list` with Java `FileTools.listFiles` output (absolute, sorted `{"entries": [...]}`).

### Key decisions
- Ported the Java body-check branch exactly (case-insensitive, same three substrings); `statusCode == 0` stays an unconditional transport-failure retry.
- `file_list`/`file_exists` MCP catalog already matched the Java `@MCPTool` names/params — no catalog change; pinned the bridge behavior with `test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart`.
- Lazy tracker verified, no code change: `IntegrationClients` builds clients on first access (failure not cached); JS `jira_*` tools resolve config per call and fail on use with `Jira not configured` — `job_runner_test` runs scripts with all `JIRA_*` blanked.
- New tests mirror the Java `RetryPolicyTest` additions (URL port digits, retry by status/body).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/js/sync_http_retry_test.dart test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local

That's a genuine behavioral divergence introduced by this port: Java only checks bodies on exceptions (error responses); Dart applies body-matching to all responses.

How impactful? GET issue from Jira: issue text/description might include "rate limit". Response 200. Client retries with backoff — up to 4 wasted sleeps (up to 60s total), result still correct. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 356
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/356
- **Title**: gh-349 parity: file_list/file_exists tools + lazy tracker in JSRunner + deterministic RetryPolicy (dm.ai#635)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-349` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +140
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T14:00:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T15:14:50Z

## PR Description

Closes #349
### What changed
Ported the deterministic-retry change from Java `RetryPolicy` (epam/dm.ai 3fa210e6, #635) and verified the other two items. `SyncRetryPolicy.isRetryableStatus`/`shouldRetry` now accept an optional response body: retryable by numeric status (429, 502/503/504) or a rate-limit/throttle body (`rate limit`, `too many requests`, `throttl`), never by substrings of an error message — the message embeds the request URL, so an ephemeral port like `50312` misfired the old `"503"` check and retried a 400. `SyncHttpClient` passes `resp.body` into the decision. Also aligned the JS-bridge `file_list` with Java `FileTools.listFiles` output (absolute, sorted `{"entries": [...]}`).

### Key decisions
- Ported the Java body-check branch exactly (case-insensitive, same three substrings); `statusCode == 0` stays an unconditional transport-failure retry.
- `file_list`/`file_exists` MCP catalog already matched the Java `@MCPTool` names/params — no catalog change; pinned the bridge behavior with `test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart`.
- Lazy tracker verified, no code change: `IntegrationClients` builds clients on first access (failure not cached); JS `jira_*` tools resolve config per call and fail on use with `Jira not configured` — `job_runner_test` runs scripts with all `JIRA_*` blanked.
- New tests mirror the Java `RetryPolicyTest` additions (URL port digits, retry by status/body).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/js/sync_http_retry_test.dart test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart
dart test            # full suite: 3646 passed, 16 skipped
crap4dart check --all  # 20 gates passed (coverage 96.7%), 1 pre-existing class_size warn
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[SyncHttpClient dispatch] --> POL[SyncRetryPolicy.shouldRetry]
  BODY[resp.body] --> POL
  POL -->|status 429/502/503/504| RETRY[retry with backoff]
  POL -->|body: rate limit / too many requests / throttl| RETRY
  POL -->|message/URL digits ignored| NORETRY[return response]
```
</details>

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local

Java `isRetryableStatus(RestClientException)` checks: status in {429,502,503,504} OR body contains rate-limit substrings — exactly what the Dart port does. In Java, isRetryable is only called for exceptions (failed requests), never for 2xx responses. In Dart's `_dispatch`, `shouldRetry` is called for every response including 2xx. The port, as applied, means: a 2xx response whose body contains "rate limit" will now be retried (up to 5 attempts with backoff). Previously 2xx never retried.

Wait — is that true? In old Dart code, `isRetryableStatus(200)` returned false → no retry. New code: `isRetryableStatus(200, body)` — status check fails, then body check: if body contains "rate limit" → true → retry. Yes, a 200 with matching body retries. That's a genuine behavioral divergence introduced by this port: Java only checks bodies on exceptions (error responses); Dart applies body-matching to all responses.

How impactful? GET issue from Jira: issue text/description might include "rate limit". Response 200. Client retries with backoff — up to 4 wasted sleeps (up to 60s total), result still correct. It's a correctness/performance issue but not data loss. Is it blocking? Given the loop is on all methods and a 200-body containing "throttl" etc. occurs in real content (e.g., searching Jira for tickets about rate limits — JQL search results returning issues whose summary contains "rate limit"!). That's plausible: `jira_search_by_jql` on text ~"rate limit" would return 200 with body containing "rate limit" → every such request retried 5x with exponential backoff up to 60s each. That's a significant latency bug for a plausible scenario.

But wait — Java parity is the spec. In Java, the check happens in `isRetryable(IOException)` — only invoked in catch block. The Dart structure differs (no exceptions, status-code based). The faithful port of intent would gate body-matching to non-2xx statuses, e.g. only when statusCode >= 400, or at least `!resp.isOk`. ## PR Description

Closes #349
### What changed
Ported the deterministic-retry change from Java `RetryPolicy` (epam/dm.ai 3fa210e6, #635) and verified the other two items. `SyncRetryPolicy.isRetryableStatus`/`shouldRetry` now accept an optional response body: retryable by numeric status (429, 502/503/504) or a rate-limit/throttle body (`rate limit`, `too many requests`, `throttl`), never by substrings of an error message — the message embeds the request URL, so an ephemeral port like `50312` misfired the old `"503"` check and retried a 400. `SyncHttpClient` passes `resp.body` into the decision. Also aligned the JS-bridge `file_list` with Java `FileTools.listFiles` output (absolute, sorted `{"entries": [...]}`).

### Key decisions
- Ported the Java body-check branch exactly (case-insensitive, same three substrings); `statusCode == 0` stays an unconditional transport-failure retry.
- `file_list`/`file_exists` MCP catalog already matched the Java `@MCPTool` names/params — no catalog change; pinned the bridge behavior with `test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart`.
- Lazy tracker verified, no code change: `IntegrationClients` builds clients on first access (failure not cached); JS `jira_*` tools resolve config per call and fail on use with `Jira not configured` — `job_runner_test` runs scripts with all `JIRA_*` blanked.
- New tests mirror the Java `RetryPolicyTest` additions (URL port digits, retry by status/body).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/js/sync_http_retry_test.dart test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart
dart test            # full suite: 3646 passed, 16 skipped
crap4dart check --all  # 20 gates passed (coverage 96.7%), 1 pre-existing class_size warn
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[SyncHttpClient dispatch] --> POL[SyncRetryPolicy.shouldRetry]
  BODY[resp.body] --> POL
  POL -->|status 429/502/503/504| RETRY[retry with backoff]
  POL -->|body: rate limit / too many requests / throttl| RETRY
  POL -->|message/URL digits ignored| NORETRY[return response]
```
</details>

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local

Closes #349
### What changed
Ported the deterministic-retry change from Java `RetryPolicy` (epam/dm.ai 3fa210e6, #635) and verified the other two items. `SyncRetryPolicy.isRetryableStatus`/`shouldRetry` now accept an optional response body: retryable by numeric status (429, 502/503/504) or a rate-limit/throttle body (`rate limit`, `too many requests`, `throttl`), never by substrings of an error message — the message embeds the request URL, so an ephemeral port like `50312` misfired the old `"503"` check and retried a 400. `SyncHttpClient` passes `resp.body` into the decision. Also aligned the JS-bridge `file_list` with Java `FileTools.listFiles` output (absolute, sorted `{"entries": [...]}`).

### Key decisions
- Ported the Java body-check branch exactly (case-insensitive, same three substrings); `statusCode == 0` stays an unconditional transport-failure retry.
- `file_list`/`file_exists` MCP catalog already matched the Java `@MCPTool` names/params — no catalog change; pinned the bridge behavior with `test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart`.
- Lazy tracker verified, no code change: `IntegrationClients` builds clients on first access (failure not cached); JS `jira_*` tools resolve config per call and fail on use with `Jira not configured` — `job_runner_test` runs scripts with all `JIRA_*` blanked.
- New tests mirror the Java `RetryPolicyTest` additions (URL port digits, retry by status/body).

```bash
dart test test/js/sync_http_retry_test.dart test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart
dart test            # full suite: 3646 passed, 16 skipped
crap4dart check --all  # 20 gates passed (coverage 96.7%), 1 pre-existing class_size warn
```

<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[SyncHttpClient dispatch] --> POL[SyncRetryPolicy.shouldRetry]
  BODY[resp.body] --> POL
  POL -->|status 429/502/503/504| RETRY[retry with backoff]
  POL -->|body: rate limit / too many requests / throttl| RETRY
  POL -->|message/URL digits ignored| NORETRY[return response]
```
</details>
